purpose: Schedule symptom measurement after a clinically meaningful laboratory flag. These rules do not infer cause, diagnosis, or treatment.

rules.reason: Iron deficiency can produce fatigue and reduced functioning; mental-health associations are inconsistent and non-causal. Measure symptoms instead of inferring them.
Ferritin rises with inflammation, so the higher WHO cutoff is used only when inflammation or infection is independently established.
This threshold indicates risk of vitamin D deficiency. Observational evidence links lower 25(OH)D with depression, but causality is not established.
Potential inadequacy is a reason to record concurrent well-being, not evidence of a mood disorder.
Record symptoms around a flagged result. No psychiatric interpretation is calculated from the laboratory value.

explicitNonRules: A percentage decline that remains inside the report-specific reference range does not by itself trigger a mental-health screen.
No questionnaire result changes a laboratory value or its reference status.
No supplement, medication, dose, or diagnosis is generated by this ruleset.
